question: Is upstream-xnu-12377 at the pinned commit the more advanced choice than 20-5-oss for ARM64 VM, Apple Silicon, and SDK work?
answer: Yes for that scope. The pin is the newer XNU and already contains the ARM64 virt images, the Apple virtual platform expert, a T8010 ramdisk path, and a later in-tree OSS SDK. The old branch's single unique commit does not raise the XNU version. It is a 9555-line squash on the older XNU whose bulk is 32-bit Cortex-A7 QEMU virt and Rockchip/Allwinner boards. Those targets are absent from the pin and are not Apple Silicon. The squash's ARM64 and SDK hunks are either already superseded on the pin or conflict with a later pin comment. One narrow arm64 fileset assert exception was not found on the pin and was not shown to be required.
method: GitHub commit API for b63b007, including the complete 134-file patch list. Read-only inspection of sources/puredarwin-baseline at e7aa00a. No fetch into either tree, no build, no boot.

unique_commit.subject: various changes (too lazy to commit properly)
unique_commit.file_list_evidence: GitHub stats.total is 9555 and the sum of per-file changes is 9555. The API returns at most 300 files; 134 is inside that cap.

classification_by_path_and_inspected_pat.note: flake.nix, nix/arm64.nix, and build.nix are counted as nix surface, but the inspected hunks in flake.nix and nix/arm64.nix add armv6/armv7 outputs, not a new aarch64 runner.

findings.old_unique_change: None. The unique commit's parent is main, and both stay on xnu-7195.121.3.
findings.pin_equivalent: The pin is xnu-12377.121.6 and the earlier comparison shows it contains main (333 ahead, 0 behind).
findings.disposition: The selected branch is the newer XNU. The old unique commit is not a newer base.

findings.topic: 32-bit QEMU virt A7 and board targets
findings.matters_to: Not Apple Silicon and not the ARM64 virt VM
findings.old_unique_change: Adds QEMU Cortex-A7 (VIRTA7) kernel, kexts, and image outputs; Rockchip RV1106/RK3506 and Allwinner SUN7I board headers; PDRockchip DWC3/DWMMC/SFC kexts; GICv2 and DW8250/PL011 early console; PDSoftRTC; arm32 libSystem export list. PDArmPlatformExpert Info.plist matches puredarwin,virt-a7, puredarwin,rv1103, and puredarwin,rk3506. New arm code is guarded with __arm__ && !__arm64__.
findings.pin_equivalent: These paths are absent from the pin: nix/pkgs/toolchain/image-arm32-virta7.nix, src/Kernel/xnu/config/MASTER.arm.virta7, PDSoftRTC.cpp, and the Rockchip kexts were not in the pin tree.
findings.disposition: Real unique work, and the largest part of the squash. It does not make 20-5-oss the more advanced Apple Silicon or ARM64 VM branch. It was not ported onto xnu-12377 by this review.

findings.old_unique_change: nix/image-contents.nix adds useRamdisk=true on the existing puredarwin-arm64-virt-minimal.img target whose boot-args already contained rd=md0. image.nix only changes SystemVersion from 11.3/20D91 to 11.4/20F71. No new arm64-virt attribute was added by the inspected flake hunks.
findings.pin_equivalent: Pin nix/image-contents.nix publishes kernel-arm64-virt, image-arm64-virt, image-arm64-virt-minimal, and arm64-virt-runner. The minimal target comment says not to pass rd=md0 because that target has no useRamdisk and IOFindBSDRoot panics. useRamdisk=true remains on netboot-arm64-virt-minimal and the T8010 ramdisk. image.nix SystemVersion is 26.5/25F74.
findings.disposition: The pin is ahead of the squash for the ARM64 VM image. Copying the old useRamdisk hunk onto the minimal image would contradict the pin's later comment.

findings.old_unique_change: No Apple AIC, DART, T-series, or Apple virtual-platform addition was in the inspected hunks. The ARM platform edits are the generic A7/Rockchip path.
findings.pin_equivalent: Pin PDArmPlatformExpert.cpp identifies an Apple virtual machine: manufacturer Apple Inc., product Apple Virtual Machine 1, description virtual machine for ARM-v8.4 with Apple Silicon extensions, compat VMA2MACOSAP/VirtualMac2,1/AppleVirtualPlatformARM, and PDAppleARMPlatformExpert with PDAppleAIC. image-contents.nix also has ramdiskArm64T8010Build for T8010.
findings.disposition: Apple Silicon VM support lives on the selected pin, not in the old unique commit.

findings.old_unique_change: Rewrites nix/pkgs/toolchain/apple-sdk-pinned.nix from a requireFile of proprietary MacOSX11.3.sdk.tar.xz into puredarwin-oss-sdk version 20.4, assembled from in-tree headers, with __DARWIN_ONLY_UNIX_CONFORMANCE forced in the generated cdefs.h and small oss-sdk stubs. cmake/crosscompile.cmake adds the same conformance macro globally and explicitly avoids __DARWIN_ONLY_64_BIT_INO_T. Also adds an 872-line arm32 libSystem export list.
findings.pin_equivalent: Pin apple-sdk-pinned.nix is already pname puredarwin-oss-sdk version 26.5. It uses lib.fileset.toSource, copies oss-sdk, forces __DARWIN_ONLY_UNIX_CONFORMANCE in cdefs.h, and includes the arm64 syscall map. The same conformance macro is set in src/Libraries/CMakeLists.txt, src/Userspace/CMakeLists.txt, and many library targets. libSystem-compat.exports and the oss-sdk tbd/header stubs from the squash are present, except sandbox.h, which the pin takes from src/Libraries/libsandbox/include/sandbox.h. libSystem.arm32-from-libdyld.exports and pd-mini-init.c are absent.
findings.disposition: The pin's SDK is a later form of the same OSS-SDK replacement. The squash is not a more advanced SDK. The arm32 export list and pd-mini-init.c are old-only and serve the 32-bit image, not the ARM64 pin.

findings.old_unique_change: src/Kernel/xnu/osfmk/arm64/arm_vm_init.c adds arm_vm_kc_prelink_text_is_exec(). When the fileset KC header is the kernel header, PRELINK_TEXT stays RWX and is not later tightened to RNX, and the empty-PRELINK_TEXT/PRELINK_INFO asserts allow that layout. The comment says kc-tools can reuse the kernel header.
findings.pin_equivalent: Pin arm_vm_prot_init and arm_vm_prot_finalize already map segPRELINKTEXTB RWX unconditionally, with a PureDarwin comment that fileset kext refinement is skipped. The pin still asserts at arm_vm_init.c:2085 that kernel PRELINK_TEXT is empty when the kernel header is in a fileset. The helper arm_vm_kc_prelink_text_is_exec is absent.
findings.disposition: The mapping behavior the squash wanted is already broader on the pin. The assert exception for a KC header that is the kernel header itself was not found. Whether current kc-tools still emits that layout was not checked.

findings.old_unique_change: pe_init.c, against the 7195 function, skips ml_static_ptovirt when deviceTreeP is already a kernel virtual address.
findings.pin_equivalent: Pin PE_init_platform assigns PE_state.deviceTreeHead from boot_args_ptr->deviceTreeP directly and does not call ml_static_ptovirt there.
findings.disposition: The old hunk does not apply to the pin's function. No missing translation workaround was established.

limits: The 134 patches were read from the GitHub commit API. The 20-5-oss tree was not checked out and its blobs were not re-hashed locally.
Path classification is from filenames plus the patches inspected for ARM64, Apple Silicon, SDK, and the arm32 board surface. The 36 other files were not reviewed line by line.
Different XNU bases mean a 7195 hunk can be inapplicable even when the same path exists on 12377. Equivalence claims are limited to the lines cited.
oss-sdk sandbox.h from the squash was not byte-compared with src/Libraries/libsandbox/include/sandbox.h.
libSystem-compat.exports exists on both sides and was not byte-compared.
No Nix evaluation, kernel build, QEMU boot, or Apple Silicon boot was run. Nothing here is a VM or hardware result.
Registry pins and checkouts were not modified.
